html_value.text: Since becoming a father, I've gained two invaluable teachers at home: my daughter and my wife. Over the past few years, they've never stopped asking me thought-provoking questions. Those questions led me to examine my own answers and, in some cases, to challenge beliefs I once considered rock-solid. Drawing on that experience, I invite you to dive into the unknown: before clicking any of the links below, try to answer each question yourself first. As you explore further pages, each one built around more questions, keep doing the same exercise and notice whether your views change along the way. At the end, compare what you believed before reading with what you believe now. The main goal of this section is to foster introspection: to slow down, think and, when necessary, rethink.

value.name: Who said indigenous peoples never had mathematical tools?
value.desc: A common misconception about indigenous communities is that they had no arithmetic tools. Yet ancient chronicles and recent studies show the opposite: they developed their own techniques for calculation and used them successfully. This page gathers that evidence for you to examine.

value.name: Who claimed that indigenous peoples are inherently different?
value.desc: Some people tend to put others down or to see themselves as superior, either because of personal preference or because they live in echo chambers where everyone agrees with them. But is there any factual basis for this idea of superiority? I have fallen into similar traps myself, whether in the excitement of a sports victory or through lessons I was wrongly taught, so here I gather research that addresses the question with evidence, for indigenous peoples and for the broader population.

value.name: Who truly discovered America (Abya Yala)?
value.desc: At first glance the answer seems obvious: history books appear to give it ready-made. But every answer depends on the worldview behind it. On this page you will compare perspectives and decide for yourself whether one of them is enough.
